description: This bar chart, titled “PHHEME” on the left and “PolitiFact” on the right, compares the accuracy percentages of a model across different configurations on two distinct misinformation detection datasets. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, spans from 75.0 to 95.0 in increments of 2.5, using a linear scale. The horizontal axis lists six categories: “Ours”, “w/o text”, “w/o select”, “w/o emotion”, and “w/o cognition”. Each category is represented by a single bar with a distinct color and its corresponding accuracy value labeled on top. In the PHHEME dataset, “Ours” achieves 89.84%, “w/o text” achieves 86.82%, “w/o select” achieves 88.80%, “w/o emotion” achieves 87.34%, and “w/o cognition” achieves 87.17%. In the PolitiFact dataset, “Ours” achieves 90.57%, “w/o comments” achieves 85.85%, “w/o text” achieves 83.02%, “w/o select” achieves 89.62%, “w/o emotion” achieves 84.91%, and “w/o cognition” achieves 87.74%. The bars are arranged in a single group per dataset, with no explicit grouping or stacking, and are not sorted. The “Ours” bar in each dataset is the tallest, while the “w/o text” bar in the PHHEME dataset and the “w/o text” bar in the PolitiFact dataset are among the shortest. The bars are colored in shades of red, orange, yellow, light blue, and dark blue, with no visual emphasis such as shading or bolding beyond the standard bar representation.
